question: What survives if the virtual Great-Pyramid operator is translated to Kamil but is NOT allowed horizontal rotation or free steering?

geometry_formulae.fixed_axis_property: For fixed site latitude, altitude and azimuth, the terrestrial axis traces one constant celestial declination as Earth rotates; time changes RA but cannot repair a declination mismatch.

primary_rigid_operators.definition: King's Chamber southern shaft reference preserved as SOUTH after translation; no azimuth rotation allowed.
51.84 degrees is a face-plane slope, not intrinsically a beam. Four cardinal slope directions are retained only as the frozen legacy structural control.
Apex beam frozen as local zenith; no steering allowed.

face_normal_secondary_control.reason: For reflection/emission physics a face-plane normal is relevant. A 51.84-degree slope has an upward outward normal 38.16 degrees above the horizon, so this is exported separately rather than silently replacing the frozen primary operator.
face_normal_secondary_control.conclusion: The physically motivated normal interpretation also fails the 0.25-degree alignment gate.

january_2026_control.principle: A full January scan cannot beat the all-time declination floor for a rigid terrestrial axis.
january_2026_control.zero_window_statement: No primary rigid operator reaches LOVE or EDEM within 0.25 degrees anywhere in January 2026; under the frozen J2000 approximation no sidereal time can repair the mismatch.

at_previous_free_azimuth_EDEM_44_5_cross.interpretation: The prior exact 44.5-degree EDEM altitude crossing existed because azimuth was allowed to rotate to about 291 degrees. The rigid SOUTH shaft is nowhere near EDEM at that instant.

isotropic_sky_null.single_target_metric: minimum absolute declination residual to any PRIMARY rigid operator axis; smaller is better
isotropic_sky_null.pair_metric: Hold LOVE-EDEM separation fixed at 90.586788289 degrees, apply a uniform random 3D rotation to the pair, require two distinct PRIMARY rigid operators, and minimize the maximum endpoint declination residual.

source_notes.source: Virginia Trimble, Astronomical Investigation Concerning the So-Called Air-Shafts of Cheops' Pyramid, 1964; Harvard Digital Giza
source_notes.supports: southern King's Chamber shaft reference angle about 44.5 degrees and north-south shaft geometry

source_notes.source: Journal of Ancient Egyptian Architecture / National Museums Scotland casing-stone measurement discussion
source_notes.supports: Great Pyramid face slope approximately 51.84 degrees

source_notes.source: Urbini et al., Geological and geophysical investigation of Kamil Crater, Egypt
source_notes.supports: moderately oblique impact from NW, approximately 30-45 degrees; published azimuth corridor about 305-340 degrees

reverse_pass.BACK: Remove free azimuth from the prior altitude-only operator.
reverse_pass.FORWARD: Translate the rigid cardinal pyramid frame to Kamil without rotation.
reverse_pass.LEFT: Test shaft 44.5, face 51.84 and apex vertical independently.
reverse_pass.RIGHT: Export face-normal physics as a secondary non-primary control rather than changing the frozen operator.
reverse_pass.FORWARD_AGAIN: Run January/all-time floors plus isotropic single-target and fixed-separation pair nulls.
reverse_pass.BACK_AGAIN: Reject alignments that require reintroducing free azimuth or steering.

next_gate.name: INDEPENDENT_EPOCH_AND_ARCHITECTURAL_UNCERTAINTY_REPLICATION_V1
only_if_continued: propagate real shaft survey uncertainty instead of one nominal 44.5-degree value
freeze one historical epoch before inspecting fit
precess celestial coordinates only after the epoch is frozen
retain Kamil impact direction as independent negative control
do not permit free azimuth without an explicit physical rotation mechanism
